name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,263

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: European law enforcer admits dropping every other cause abandoned by English

indicators.note: losing every second letter of admits leaves only the odd-numbered ones standing
the word for cause is deserted by the English letter, which therefore leaves it

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of admits
to mean is to cause or bring about, as in 'this will mean trouble'
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A European police officer lets an argument slip half-heard, and the English abandon their cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean in the sense of cause is the verb in 'this will mean trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: An amtman is a district magistrate or bailiff in Germany and Scandinavia, an official who administers local justice.

clue.text: Magistrature, sending away soldiers, runs and engineers Nairobi minibus

indicators.note: sending away the soldiers, runs and engineers removes those letters from magistrature

blocks.note: taken as written
GIs are American soldiers
R for runs, from cricket scoring
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A magistrate's office in Kenya dismisses troops and engineers, perhaps to sort out the city's buses.
explanation.walkthrough: Take G, I and S, then one R, then the final RE out of MAGISTRATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A matatu is the shared minibus taxi that serves as everyday public transport across Kenya.

clue.text: Sporty singer once hastened to cover unknown, mostly to augment aged leader in Genesis

indicators.note: the word for hastened wraps around the unknown, covering it
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for augment goes

blocks.note: Mel C was Sporty Spice of the Spice Girls
hied is an old past tense meaning hurried
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
to eke is to add to or stretch out

explanation.surface: A former Spice Girl rushes to boost an elderly frontman of the band Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genesis' reads like the rock band, but it is the first book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Melchizedek is the king of Salem and priest who blesses Abraham in the Genesis narrative.

clue.text: Economy’s foremost in political gathering for miners, according to figures

indicators.note: foremost picks out only the leading letter of economy
in places the economy letter inside the miners' political gathering

blocks.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers
a rally is a mass political meeting
first letter of economy

explanation.surface: At a union meeting for miners, economic matters come first, judging by the statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: The E sits between the union and its rally, at the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerally is an adverb meaning in terms of numbers or by count, which is going by the figures.

clue.text: In returning characters framed by HL, don’t mention a rebel

indicators.note: returning sends the run of characters back the way it came
In places the omission-plus-a inside the run of characters

blocks.note: the alphabet letters sitting between H and L
to omit something is to leave it unsaid
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is warned not to mention a rebel to the letters HL, perhaps a cryptic set of initials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters framed by HL' means the letters of the alphabet that lie between H and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A komitaji was a member of an armed Balkan revolutionary band, an insurgent fighting Ottoman rule.

clue.text: Stab in bar certainly upset Tanzanian accustomed to grazing

indicators.note: in puts the word for stab inside the word for bar
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: an inn is a pub, a bar
to have a stab is to have a go
OK as an agreeing 'certainly'

explanation.surface: A knifing in a bar has certainly upset someone from Tanzania who is used to being pushed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanzanian' looks like a person; it is an animal of the East African plains.
explanation.definitionFit: The kongoni is the Coke's hartebeest, a grazing antelope of the savannas of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Wet and wild primitive instincts

blocks.note: mad as in wild or frenzied
the id is Freud's name for the instinctive part of the mind

explanation.surface: Basic urges described as soggy and untamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Madid is a rare literary adjective meaning moist or damp, from Latin madidus.

clue.text: Piece of safety glass old mug handled more than once

definitions.text: old mug handled more than once

indicators.note: a piece of the following words is cut out of them, spanning the word break

blocks.note: the end of safety and the start of glass

explanation.surface: A shard of toughened glass from an antique tankard that has passed through many hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handled more than once' sounds like much use; it means having several handles.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyg is an old English drinking cup with two or more handles, so it is literally multiply handled.

clue.text: Spread soft cheese from India, saving last for bearer there

indicators.note: saving here means except, so the final letter of the cheese is left out

blocks.note: jam is something spread on bread
paneer is a fresh Indian cheese

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a spread made with Indian paneer, keeping the last bit back for a porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to India, so the definition is an Indian bearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jampanee was a porter who carried a jampan, a kind of sedan chair used in India.

clue.text: Market trader’s barely credible months in traditional clinic

indicators.note: in puts the unlikely-sounding months inside the old-fashioned clinic

blocks.note: a tall story is hard to believe
m is the abbreviation for month
san is an old-fashioned short form of sanatorium

explanation.surface: A street seller claims an implausibly long stay at an old-style clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallman is someone who keeps a stall, especially a seller in a street market.

clue.text: Investigator high in second union

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
game that is high is gamy, strong-smelling from hanging

explanation.surface: A detective on a high during his second wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' tempts as drugged or elated; here it is the smell of hung game.
explanation.definitionFit: Digamy is a remarriage after the death or divorce of a first spouse, so a second marriage.

clue.text: Chapter number overwhelms person preparing plate for printing?

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the number swallows the chapter

blocks.note: a number is something that numbs, and ether was an anaesthetic
C is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: The size of a print run overwhelms the person getting the printing plate ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a count; read it as numb-er, something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An etcher bites a design into a metal plate with acid so it can be inked and printed.

clue.text: In Saskatchewan this Canadian duck would be disposed of with a screech

indicators.note: set inside Saskatchewan's letters the answer would make the longer phrase, so those letters come off

blocks.note: SK is the postal abbreviation for the province
something sold has been disposed of
a squawk is a harsh cry

explanation.surface: A wild duck in a Canadian prairie province would be sold off amid a lot of noisy squawking.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: write the answer inside Saskatchewan's two-letter postal code and you get a phrase meaning sold with a screech.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldsquaw is the former North American name for the long-tailed duck, a noisy sea duck of northern waters.

clue.text: For military clerk it’s a thrill to capture hostile doctor

indicators.note: the word for a thrill holds the other pieces captive inside it

blocks.note: a quiver is a tremble of excitement
ill as in ill will, unfriendly
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: An army desk clerk gets a kick out of arresting an unfriendly doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A quill-driver is a scornful term for a clerk or scribbler who pushes a pen for a living.

clue.text: Idol with two heads to display in staggering size: are they made of gold?

indicators.note: staggering means reeling unsteadily, so the letters of size totter into a new order
in puts the idol and the display inside the reworked size

blocks.note: a lion is a celebrity idol; give it a second head letter
to air something is to show it off
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge two-headed idol on display prompts the question whether it is solid gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made of gold' looks like a golden statue, but it is the idiom for being extremely rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Zillionaires are people of immense wealth, the sort said to be made of money or rolling in it.

clue.text: Origin of psyche quickly arising in this collective consciousness?

indicators.note: origin of means the starting letter of psyche
in a down clue arising means reading upwards, so those letters run backwards

blocks.note: first letter of psyche
soon as in before long
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Asks whether the mind's beginnings springing up fast belong in a shared human awareness.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial letter and the word for quickly are reversed together, so the P ends up after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Teilhard de Chardin's noosphere is the sphere of shared human thought enveloping the Earth, a planetary mind.

clue.text: Constrain one to be in dock, which might be a squash

indicators.note: to be in the dock means sitting inside it, so those letters are placed within

blocks.note: to dock is to cut, as with a tail or wages
to curb is to restrain
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A defendant is restrained and put in the dock, which might feel like a squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests a courtroom; it is the verb meaning to cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A cucurbit is any plant of the gourd family, such as pumpkin, marrow or courgette, so a squash is one example.

clue.text: Undo holy class, wanting learner to disrupt this?

definitions.text: Undo holy class, wanting learner to disrupt this?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the learner letter is missing from the phrase
to disrupt is to throw into disorder, so the remaining letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the three words taken as written
L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: A mischievous pupil who wants to break up a religious lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one L from UNDO HOLY CLASS and rearrange; the whole clue also describes a child itching to wreck a church class.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunday school gives religious lessons to children, a holy class that a restless young learner might well want to disrupt.

clue.text: Effort to deceive coming our way

blocks.note: to con is to trick
something coming at us is heading our way

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to fool us as they head in our direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Conatus is a philosophical term for striving or the inclination to act, the impulse to make an attempt.

clue.text: Greeting to a suitable victim, starting with the conclusion that’ll go over a woman’s head

definitions.text: that’ll go over a woman’s head

indicators.note: the final letter is brought round to begin the word instead

blocks.note: hi is a casual hello
a mark is the target of a con

explanation.surface: A con artist hails an easy target, a remark that goes right over her head.
explanation.walkthrough: HI MARK has its last letter moved to the front. 'go over a woman's head' sounds like failing to be understood; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A khimar is a long veil or headscarf worn by some Muslim women, draped over the head and shoulders.

clue.text: Yellow-grey horse jerkily unsaddles related ones

blocks.note: a horse that bucks leaps and jerks to throw its rider
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A dun-coloured horse throws off members of its own family.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckskin is a horse with a tan or yellowish coat and black mane, tail and lower legs.

clue.text: Frozen dessert provided jamminess but not cold, contrarily

indicators.note: but not cold means the cold letter is excluded from the luck word
contrarily means the opposite way round, so the whole string is read in reverse

blocks.note: if as in provided that
jammy is British slang for lucky, so jamminess is luck
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An ice cream offered on the condition of sticky fingers, though not too chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain jammy means fortunate. IF plus LUK reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kulfi is a dense South Asian ice cream made from slowly reduced milk, set in moulds.

clue.text: Greek sceptic’s years between two forms of his 17th letter

indicators.note: between sets the years in the space separating the two letter forms

blocks.note: the capital form of the Greek seventeenth letter looks like a P
yr is the abbreviation for year
the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet spelt out

explanation.surface: A Greek philosopher's age falls between two versions of one letter of his alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek seventeenth letter's capital looks like a Latin P, and its name is spelt out as the other form.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrrho of Elis founded ancient Greek scepticism, teaching suspension of judgement about all knowledge.

clue.text: Radius not within M25 for one marking departure date

indicators.note: not within means the radius letter is taken out from inside the road

blocks.note: the M25 motorway is the London Orbital, a ring road
r is the symbol for radius

explanation.surface: A distance not inside London's ring road, measured to mark the day someone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway ringing London. 'departure' looks like travel; it is death.
explanation.definitionFit: Obital relates to an obit, the anniversary of a person's death, so it commemorates the day someone died.

clue.text: Rise of soft Tory is a worry for the country

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads from the bottom up, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a wet was a moderate Conservative opposed to Thatcher's hard line

explanation.surface: Political commentary: a resurgent moderate Conservative is bad news for the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the country' looks political; it marks a rural dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tew is a dialect word for fuss or anxiety, used in provincial speech as a noun for trouble.

clue.text: The box containing western evangelical’s case sensitive music book

indicators.note: containing means the box holds the following pieces inside it
the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of evangelical are kept

blocks.note: the box is slang for television
W for western
outer letters of evangelical
emo is an emotional, confessional style of rock

explanation.surface: A television holds a cowboy preacher's suitcase and a tender songbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelvemo is the duodecimo book size, a volume of pages folded twelve to a sheet.

clue.text: Scots secretly love to fill mugs up in turn

indicators.note: the love word goes inside to fill the hollow of the other word
turned round, the combined letters are read the other way

blocks.note: to mug up and to swot both mean to cram for an exam
love is a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Scots quietly use affection to fill beer mugs in rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' marks a Scottish word; 'mugs up' is the verb for cramming, not drinking vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowlins is a Scots adverb meaning by stealth or covertly, done on the quiet.

clue.text: Indications of hesitation when catching first of repetitions or deviations

indicators.note: catching means the hesitation sounds hold the next pieces inside
first of takes only the opening letter of repetitions

blocks.note: er is the sound of hesitating
first letter of repetitions
taken as written

explanation.surface: A talk is full of ums and ers, plus repetitions and digressions, like a game show's list of faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors are mistakes, departures from what is correct or intended.
